All our applications are **free, open-source and require no registration**.
Source code lives on [github.com/l2ib-lab](https://github.com/l2ib-lab).

::: {.callout-note}
## Stable links
Each app has a permanent L2IB address of the form
`https://www.l2ib.fr/tools/<app-name>/`.
**Cite that address in papers**, never the hosting provider's URL — it lets us
change host without breaking published links.
:::

---

::: {.app-card}
### FIBOM-AI

::: {.app-tagline}
Machine-learning prediction of grade 2–3 bone marrow fibrosis from a routine
complete blood count.
:::

::: {.app-meta}
**Model** XGBoost · **Training cohort** ~2,000 patients, French university
hospitals · **AUC** 0.96 (training) · **Inputs** 27 CBC variables + age ·
**Requires** `R >= 4.1.0` for local use
:::

FIBOM-AI estimates the probability of significant (grade 2–3) bone marrow
fibrosis using only a complete blood count and the patient's age — data already
available for every patient, with no additional test. The app reports both a
general prediction and a stricter "confident" prediction based on clinical
cutoffs.

[▶ Launch the app](fibom-ai/index.qmd){.btn-app .btn-launch}
[Source code](https://github.com/VincentAlcazer/FIBOM-AI){.btn-app}
[Publication](#){.btn-app}
[Cite](#citing-fibom-ai){.btn-app}

::: {.disclaimer}
**Research tool.** FIBOM-AI is intended for research and educational purposes.
It does not constitute a medical device and must not be used as a substitute for
clinical judgement, a bone marrow biopsy, or the advice of a qualified
practitioner. No data entered in the application is stored by the L2IB team.
:::

#### Citing FIBOM-AI {#citing-fibom-ai}

```bibtex
@article{alcazer_fibomai,
  author  = {Alcazer, Vincent and others},
  title   = {FIBOM-AI: machine learning prediction of bone marrow fibrosis
             from complete blood count},
  journal = {TODO},
  year    = {TODO},
```

:::

## Hosting

Our applications are [Shiny](https://shiny.posit.co) apps written in R and
deployed on [Posit Connect Cloud](https://connect.posit.cloud) directly from
their GitHub repositories. Every push to `main` redeploys the app.

To run any of them locally:

```r
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("l2ib-lab/<repo>")
# then follow the run_app() instruction in the repo README
```
